text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak's talks with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl concentrate on the peace process, international issues and boosting bilateral relations. Mubarak came back home yesterday evening after a two-day business visit.
- Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to discuss today means to save peace. Arafat is expected in Cairo today.
- The Capital Market Authority approved the establishment of 130 new firms through the issuance of a total of 48.5 million shares through public offers.
- The Federal Bureau for Investigation denies the death of the blind Sheikh Omar Abdel Rahman, detained in a U.S. prison.
- Mubarak to inaugurate a new underground line on October 1. Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri and eight ministers witnessed the first operation trial yesterday.

- Suez Canal Chairman General Ahmed Fadhel says, "Navigation has not been disrupted. A report by a foreign news agency is untrue." Fadhel said the unnamed agency reported on Monday that passaging through the canal was disrupted after a collision between between two ships at the mouth of the canal in Port Said.
